title: AI Business Applications, ERP, and CRM Consulting

questions.question: Why do ERP and CRM AI use cases need system-boundary review?
options: Because AI output depends on workflow context, master data, exceptions, and integrations
Because master data ownership is irrelevant
Because business applications never have exceptions
questions.explanation: Business application AI depends on systems, data ownership, workflows, and integration constraints.

questions.question: Which signal is part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Master data dependency affects the design and ownership of business application AI.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked business application AI fit plan with controls
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks scenarios and recommends controls before solution design.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: System boundaries make the AI use case realistic and reviewable.

questions.question: When should a business application AI idea go to solution design workshop?
options: When value and integration risk are high and multiple system signals are present
Only when no transaction context exists
Only when the integration is ignored
Never; a prompt demo is enough
questions.explanation: High-value, high-risk business app use cases need structured design review.

questions.question: What should be clear before proposing AI in ERP or CRM workflows?
options: System boundary, data owner, exception rule, and integration note
questions.explanation: These controls keep business application AI grounded in real workflows.
